The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: A pentagon. Going from the bottom left corner and working clockwise, the corners are labeled as A, E, D, C, and B. There is a line drawn from A to D, and also from A to C.]

What is the sum of all the interior angles of pentagon ABCDE?
Show your work.

Answer: ____

Figure, described in words:
A pentagon ABCDE with vertices labeled clockwise starting from the bottom left: A at the bottom left, E at the middle left, D at the top apex, C at the middle right, and B at the bottom right. Two internal line segments are drawn from vertex A: one segment connects A to D, and another connects A to C, dividing the interior of the pentagon into three triangles: triangle AED, triangle ADC, and triangle ABC.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: The pentagon has 5 sides, so it can be divided into 5 − 2 = 3 triangles by drawing diagonals from one vertex. The lines from A to D and from A to C split the pentagon into triangles AED, ADC, and ABC. Each triangle has interior angles summing to 180°, so the sum of the interior angles of the pentagon is 3 × 180° = 540°. Check using the formula (n − 2) × 180° with n = 5: (5 − 2) × 180° = 3 × 180° = 540°. Answer: 540°
